review: Reviewed account portal changes and request/render lifecycle, its test suite, the new first-party GCN source connection and both GCN tests. Previously reviewed account-room, authenticator and six billing components are exact-hash checked against the latest candidate index.

Website identity, verified factor enrollment, room-session enrollment, device credential/text permission, source credential access and paid/provider authority remain separate UI controls. The page labels managed membership, voice and Agent API funding as not publicly available; sandbox controls require admitted status responses.

Reproduced and fixed a late independent ledger read restoring cap controls after website sign-out. Account refresh increments an observation epoch; cap reads capture it and a latest-read generation, with guards after body reads and errors. Unmount invalidates both. A regression issues a cap read, signs out and resolves the old response; controls remain absent.

Returned legacy checkout selectors remain untrusted until a same-account reconciliation response. Browser intent identity is reused for an uncertain request; Stripe checkout/management links enforce HTTPS host and omit userinfo. Usage reservations and estimates are displayed separately from own-key usage and processor invoices.

GCN credentials remain in controlled password inputs and are cleared before submission, refresh or account invalidation. Explicit updates include expected profile identity; late account responses are ignored. Public retained data, saved-inactive credentials and bounded private source leases are distinct. No source save itself grants paid reasoning, Discord delivery or game authority.

GCN schema and server fixture builder were read as test dependencies but are not exported by this web cohort. The test calls a pure status constructor with explicit storage availability; database/save/encryption functions are not invoked. Synthetic credentials only.
limits: Private unfrozen source proposal; no publication, sign-in, checkout, provider/source connection, room action or device revocation was performed.

Twenty-three mocked tests cover account-page behavior and GCN credential UI. They do not prove live Auth0/Stripe/GCN service access, customer funding, encrypted storage, private-worker expiry, installed native or signed-update acceptance.
The page suite mocks Google sign-in and authenticator rendering. Room owner-presence/invite integration and private GCN activation paths are read/compiled but not qualified end-to-end by these tests.

Only independent cap observations gained account-epoch isolation. Other page refresh/mutation/poll completions and TOTP state across account replacement remain separate lifecycle acceptance concerns; no broad account-concurrency claim.
Support contact review inherited from capped membership remains in the final owner publication candidate. Shared/server dependencies and the remaining web changes still require their own review.
